title: The cracked sea-stack: the textbook-correct rule against the one shipped
question: Which of these reads as rock standing at rest, rather than rock being chewed?
context_md:
Following your question about why the stack is still cracked. It is a real bug, and I want your eye before I decide not to fix it.

The rule that cracks it asks whether a piece's weight sits within the middle third of the ground it stands on. It measures that offset **from whichever cell it happens to be looking at** rather than from the middle of the footing — so a piece sitting dead centre on its own base is judged to be toppling. Measured: a cell standing on a footing six wide, carrying a load whose centre of mass is two tenths of a cell off dead centre, crushed for an offset of 2.3 against an allowance of 1.

One of the panes below is the rule as shipped. The other is the same rule with that arithmetic corrected — which is unambiguously the right formula, and which I am proposing **not** to ship, because it loses 40% more rock and to my eye leaves the stack worse. Both runs are idle: no verb of any kind, same seed, same frames.

If the corrected one looks better to you, I will keep going on it — my reading of these two images is the thing I am least sure of.
